patterns: News-jack one-line question: Cardone's 'Would you invest 1,000,000 in Anthropic?' hit 57.0k with 455 replies on the IPO news. His wordier version ('If you were down to your last 1,000,000…') stalled at 7.4k. Keep it short, tie it to the headline, and make people pick a side. Keywords: would you invest, 1,000,000, how high does it go.

Benchmark questions are confirmed: HughInvests' 'You're 32, earning £44k, renting, no property. Are you doing alright?' went from 8.6k to 25.2k (+16.6k) and is now a star. Keywords: are you doing alright, renting, no property, by now.

The regional call-out keeps compounding: @justhomesgroup's 'To the men in my DMs' went from 97.4k to 108.2k (+10.8k). Cardone's 'act don't panic' also added 10.2k (53.5k). The 'choose ONE' fork is basically flat (+0.6k at #1), so retire it.

Avoid these: persona bait ('I'm 60, retired from Berkshire… $330,000/month', 71.1k, only 44 likes) implies returns and is low-trust. Cardone's political confession (77.6k) is off-brand. Ben Kelly's greentext case study ('> Be Scott and Crystal… own a rental in Kentucky') got 15 bookmarks on 3.5k. It's an emerging save-worthy format.

narrative_synthesis: Today's meta: (1) a short news-jack 'would you invest $1M in X?' question, (2) 'are you doing alright?' benchmark questions, now proven, and (3) greentext case studies that get saved. Drafts: a $1M IPO-vs-Philly-rentals fork, a hypothetical house-hacking greentext, and a wholesale 65% gut-check question.

drafts.draft_en:
You've got $1,000,000.

A) All of it in the hottest AI IPO
B) All of it in Philly rental properties

You have to pick one, and you can't sell for 10 years.

Which one, and why?
drafts.pattern: News-jack one-line fork (Cardone's 'Would you invest 1,000,000 in Anthropic?', 57.0k and 455 replies). Localized to Philly rentals. No returns are promised; it's an opinion question.
drafts.video_tip: Selfie-style, 8–10s, on a Philly rowhome block. Hold up one finger for A (AI IPO) and two for B (Philly rentals), then say 'Pick one. Comments.' Burn in captions. Pin a reply asking what they'd do with the cash flow vs the shares.

drafts.draft_en:
> Be Tasha (hypothetical)
> 31, nurse in Philly, renting a 1-bed
> Buys a duplex with a low-down-payment owner-occupant loan
> Lives in one unit, rents out the other
> Tenant's rent covers part of the mortgage
> Her housing cost drops while she builds equity

That's house hacking.

Would you live next door to your tenant?
drafts.pattern: Greentext case study (Ben Kelly's '> Be Scott and Crystal', 15 bookmarks on 3.5k). Labeled hypothetical, with no specific return or dollar promises.
drafts.video_tip: Screen-record the text being typed line by line over B-roll of a Philly duplex front door. 15s. End on the question in big type. Pin a reply: 'Would you, yes or no?'

drafts.draft_en:
Wholesale gut check:

ARV: $200K
Repairs: $40K

What's the most you'd pay for it?

My rule for flips: purchase + repairs, all in, at or under 65% of ARV.

$200K x 65% = $130K all in
$130K − $40K repairs = $90K max offer

What's your number?
drafts.pattern: Benchmark question ('are you doing alright?', 8.6k to 25.2k) plus a reply-bait answer. Uses Bar's 65% rule correctly: purchase plus repairs vs ARV, for wholesale/flip deals only.
drafts.video_tip: Whiteboard or notes app, 15–20s. Write ARV and repairs, then pause and ask 'what do you offer?' Do the 65% math live. End with 'Drop your number below.' Burn in captions.
